newsitem.title: USA: Miami air cargo flat in September.
newsitem.headline: Miami air cargo flat in September.

text.p: Cargo through Miami International Airport in September edged down slightly from the year-ago volumes, but for the first nine months MIA handled nearly 8 percent more freight than the same period last year, according to statistics from the Dade County Aviation Department.
"After about nine months of strong growth, we can expect to see some flattening in the growth curve," said Emir Pineda, MIA cargo development officer.
Total cargo, including mail, amounted to 148,897 tons in September, down 0.46 percent from the year earlier, the Dade County figures show.
International cargo totaled 120,969 tons, up 0.65 percent from September 1995. Domestic cargo was 27,928 tons, off 4.99 percent from the year ago.
The number of flights in and out of MIA was down 10 percent "and that affects cargo too," said Pineda.
For the first nine months, all cargo amounted to 1,366,419 tons, up 7.95 percent from the first three quarters of 1995.

International cargo amounted to 1,087,538 tons for the year-to-date to Sept 30, up 6.24 percent, while domestic cargo rose 15.18 percent to 278,881 tons in the period. -- Miami news bureau, 305-374-5013
